note: Holdings-relevant market news, researched daily by the intel agent (multi-theme sweep: precious metals, HK tech, SGX/Singapore, rare earths, macro) with sources. The "actionable" line relates each item to this specific portfolio. Monday 20 July early-SGT run: US/Asia markets have not traded since the Friday 17 July close, so levels reflect that close; refreshed with the newest catalysts (Lynas CEO handover, SG-REIT earnings season, the 28-29 July FOMC in focus). Not financial advice.

items.headline: Silver closes Friday at 8-month lows (~$55.60) — still can't crack $60, ~54% below January's record
items.summary: Silver ended the week around $55.60/oz, fresh 8-month lows, after failing repeatedly to reclaim $60; it is roughly 54% below its late-January all-time high of ~$121.62. The metal fell even as the US-Iran war raged, trading as a rate/industrial asset rather than a safe haven — a firm dollar and revived rate-hike fears from the oil spike overwhelmed the geopolitical bid. J.P. Morgan still models silver averaging ~$81/oz for 2026 on a widening structural deficit.
items.actionable: The book's highest-beta pain point: keep leverage sized so the break to 8-month lows can't force liquidation, and let the oil-inflation impulse and July FOMC clear before any deep-value re-entry — $58-60 is the level a base would need to reclaim.

items.headline: Gold steadies right at $4,000 (~$4,017, +1% Friday) as PBoC buys a 20th straight month
items.summary: Spot gold firmed ~1% Friday to close around $4,017/oz, stabilizing at the $4,000 shelf after its biggest weekly loss in six — roughly 24% below January's peak above $5,300. The war's oil spike and a firm dollar (DXY ~100.9) capped the rebound, but central-bank demand is a genuine floor: the PBoC added 14.93 tonnes in June (20th straight month) and ~89% of central banks expect to keep accumulating. Goldman's year-end target sits ~$4,900, J.P. Morgan's Q4 view ~$4,500 — both above spot.
items.actionable: Central-bank buying is a floor near ~$4,000 for the GDX/miner sleeve, but don't expect gold to rescue silver — both hinge on the oil-inflation impulse and the 28-29 July FOMC.

items.headline: US airstrikes on Iran enter a 6th night; WTI jumps to ~$82.5, Brent ~$88 on Hormuz fears
items.summary: US CENTCOM ran a sixth consecutive night of strikes and reimposed a naval blockade after Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks; WTI spiked ~4.5% Friday to ~$82.47 (a 5-week high) and Brent to ~$88.09, up double digits on the week. Qatar and Kuwait fended off fresh attacks. The VIX rose ~12% to 18.8 and the S&P fell ~1% as the war-premium built. Energy is now the leading S&P sector.
items.actionable: The oil premium lifts energy but is precisely what is crushing the metals book and pressuring SGX REITs via inflation — do NOT add levered silver on the geopolitical spike; a Hormuz ceasefire headline is the fast-reversal risk in both directions.

items.headline: June CPI cools to 3.5% (core 2.6%) — softer than expected, but the oil spike muddies the Fed path
items.summary: US headline CPI fell 0.4% m/m — the biggest monthly drop since 2020 — cutting annual inflation to 3.5% from 4.2% in May, with core flat at 2.6% y/y, both below consensus. Falling energy/gasoline drove the decline, but energy is still +15.7% y/y and the Iran-driven crude spike clouds the read: some post-print commentary even floats September hike risk, while the June dot-plot skewed hawkish (no cuts near-term).
items.actionable: Cooler core is supportive for metals and risk, but higher-for-longer keeps the big cash pile earning ~3.6-4% with no urgency to redeploy before the 28-29 July FOMC — the cleanest metals-positive would be an Iran de-escalation that deflates oil.

items.headline: Semis rout deepens: SOX -11% on the month, SMH -9% in four weeks on AI-capex-peak fears
items.summary: The semiconductor complex was the market's biggest loser this window — SOX down ~11% on the month, SMH ~9% over four weeks and ~20% off the 22 June peak — on fears hyperscaler AI-capex spending has peaked (Micron -8%, Intel -4%). Michael Burry's fresh NVDA/MU/AMAT shorts are working. Money rotated out of chips into energy, financials and industrials, dragging the S&P to 7,457.69 (-1.01% Fri) and Nasdaq to 25,520 — but breadth broadened (~68.6% above the 200-DMA, best since February), so it reads as a rotation, not a broad breakdown.
items.actionable: Don't catch the semis knife (SMH/SMIC 0981.HK); the silver lining is the rotation is INTO energy/financials/industrials with ex-tech breadth healthy at ~69% >200-DMA, and the >$400B 2026 hyperscaler capex is the 12m floor.

items.headline: Hang Seng Tech rips ~5.5% — best week in 14 months; Tencent +10% on a WeChat AI agent
items.summary: HSTECH climbed ~5.5% (its strongest week in 14 months) and the Hang Seng +3.2% as capital rotated out of AI hardware into internet/application names. Tencent leapt ~10.5% after reports it moved closer to launching an AI agent for WeChat's ~1.4bn users; Alibaba and Meituan also surged. The move coincides with Tencent's rolling buyback (~1.59m shares repurchased 6-9 July, ~32 consecutive days for ~34.5M shares under its 10% mandate).
items.actionable: Directly bullish for the Tencent core — the WeChat AI-agent monetization narrative is exactly the re-rating catalyst, and the buyback bid is near-mechanical; ride the internet-over-hardware rotation while it runs.

items.headline: China Q2 GDP slows to 4.3% — weakest since 2022, first miss of its own target since Covid
items.summary: China grew 4.3% y/y in Q2 (down from 5.0% in Q1, below the 4.5% consensus) — the first miss of its target range since the pandemic. A deep property downturn (investment -18%) and weak domestic demand dragged; fixed-asset investment fell 5.7% in H1, offset by exports surging ~27% on semiconductors and computer parts.
items.actionable: Soft growth is a near-term headwind for the HK-tech consumer names but raises the odds of forceful PBoC/fiscal stimulus — the key upside optionality; watch for a policy response as the FXI/HK-tech swing factor.

items.headline: STI hits a record ~5,561; DBS becomes first SGX stock past S$200bn market cap
items.summary: The Straits Times Index set a fresh record of 5,561.42 on 15 July (up ~33% y/y), driven by the three banks (DBS, OCBC, UOB) that make up over half the benchmark. DBS became the first SGX-listed stock to exceed S$200bn market capitalisation. The rally leaves the lenders extended into results.
items.actionable: The SGX bank sleeve is at all-time highs and doing the heavy lifting for the book — but with lenders extended at ~2.2x book into ~6 August results, watch valuation/momentum and favor S-REITs on any lower-SORA relief.

items.headline: Singapore REIT earnings season opens: Keppel REIT & Mapletree Logistics report; data-centre and SG-centric names resilient
items.summary: S-REIT results kicked off in the week of 14 July, with Keppel REIT and Mapletree Logistics Trust reporting and CapitaLand Ascott Trust divesting a Tianjin property. Singapore-centric and data-centre names held up best — CICT and Keppel DC REIT posted FY DPU growth of ~+6.4% and ~+10% respectively at ~96% occupancy — but higher borrowing costs and the oil-driven inflation impulse continue to pressure the broader sector, which lagged the bank-led STI in H1.
items.actionable: Within the S-REIT/developer sleeve, favor Singapore-centric, data-centre and strong-balance-sheet names over rate-sensitive ones while the Iran oil premium and the 28-29 July FOMC keep SORA/borrowing costs elevated; the banks remain the STI's engine.

items.headline: US extends floor-price guarantees to favored ex-China rare-earth suppliers, including Lynas
items.summary: The US has begun offering price-guarantee (floor-price) support to favored non-China suppliers including Lynas, extending the model set by the DoD-MP Materials partnership. Lynas' Malaysia refinery is the largest outside China and the first to produce commercial dysprosium oxide. On 7 July Lynas also signed a deal with South Korea's JS Link to build a 3,000tpa NdFeB magnet plant in Kuantan.
items.actionable: Government floor-price support de-risks the ex-China basket by capping the 'China floods the market' bear case — watch REMX/MP/LYC.AX pullbacks as cash-funded scale-in candidates (6680.HK carries the export-cap headwind).

items.headline: Lynas CEO Amanda Lacaze steps down; ops chief Pol Le Roux takes interim reins
items.summary: Long-serving Lynas Rare Earths CEO Amanda Lacaze stepped down on 1 July, handing control to operations chief Pol Le Roux on an interim basis while a permanent successor is sought. The succession uncertainty weighed on the VanEck Rare Earth ETF (REMX) in early July, only partly offset by MP Materials' record Q1 (~49% revenue surge on its DoD price floor and Apple magnet offtake). China's continued export-control enforcement (MP and USA Rare Earth remain on the June entity list; licensing now reaches any foreign product with ≥0.1% Chinese-origin rare earths) keeps the ex-China supply thesis structurally intact.
items.actionable: Adds execution/succession risk to the only commercial-scale ex-China NdPr + heavy-rare-earth producer — a reason to favor MP (record Q1, DoD floor) over Lynas within the cash-funded rare-earth watchlist until a permanent CEO is named.

items.headline: Bitcoin pinned near $64k after record June ETF outflows; softer CPI and a Japan BTC ETF give a bounce
items.summary: BTC traded around $64,400 into the Fri 17 July close, coiling in a $56-64k range after Bitcoin ETFs posted their worst month on record in June (~$4.5bn outflows). Softer CPI and a new Japan Bitcoin ETF gave a mid-week bounce, but Iran headlines capped it. Crypto Fear & Greed sits at 25 (Fear); ETH ~$1,850. BTC is trading as a high-beta risk asset tied to the rate path.
items.actionable: Any crypto sleeve stays small and range-bound into the 28-29 July FOMC; the softer CPI and building regulatory tailwinds (US CLARITY Act, Japan reclassification) are structural positives, but June ETF outflows show institutional caution.

items.headline: Global fund flows turn defensive: cash +$39.5B and IG bonds +$31.3B lead; gold/energy bleed
items.summary: BofA's latest weekly 'Flow Show' (EPFR) showed a defensive-not-bearish rotation into cash (+$39.5B) and investment-grade bonds (+$31.3B), with record-pace tech inflows even as gold, energy and materials saw outflows. BofA private clients logged their first net US-equity inflow in five weeks (hedge-fund-led), while Financials saw heavy selling and buybacks fell to a 6-week low.
items.actionable: The flow tide is against gold/energy and toward cash and quality credit — validates keeping the big cash pile as dry powder near ~4% yield while the metals sleeve bases; the crowded tech/AI inflows are the crowded-trade risk on the semis unwind.
